did: Read lab/TASKS.md, tasks/constraints/spec.md, tasks/constraints/dev.json and the json/regex checker code plus norm() in lab/core.py
Wrote 21 single-mode strict-JSON tasks g1-01..g1-21 (7 easy, 7 medium, 7 hard) with a Python build script
Validated with lab/validate_tasks.py: 21/21 valid (every reference passes, every negative fails)

medium: string-vs-number with leading zero and decimal
array of objects dropping a field
alphabetically sorted list inside an object
date split with month name to number
apply a correction to get the final state
hard: min/max/difference with lowercase and uppercase rules
array of objects sorted by price
sum + boolean budget comparison + most expensive item

answer_verification: Every derived value (sums, counts, sorts, filters, min/max, gap, month number, minute conversions, grouping, boolean comparison) is computed by Python in the build script from the same data structures that generate the prompt text, so the prompt and the expected answer cannot drift apart. Copied values were read back from the printed references.
checker_notes: All tasks use the json checker with strict true plus keys/equals for objects or list_len/value for arrays
json.equals on strings is case-insensitive, so case rules (g1-07, g1-17) have an extra case-sensitive regex
Python treats true == 1, so boolean and null fields (g1-03, g1-09, g1-20) have an extra regex for the literal true/false/null

Each negative is a near miss breaking one rule: number as string, extra key, wrong case, unsorted, pre-correction value, filtered instead of full sum, missing group member, wrong boolean, unconverted duration
not_done: No model pilot was run on these tasks (held-out by instruction), so the easy/medium/hard labels are estimates from the spec's baseline guidance, not measured.
